NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5080, GPU-b28db334-b11d-c7ec-1e24-d2f408b0a55c, 615.78.08, 14259 MiB, 38, 465 MHz, 15001 MHz, 360.00 W

method: Two warmups and five measurements per request size and mode. Paired mode order alternates; each pair uses the same public test seed, stream ID 17 and initial u32 word offset 15.

Both modes produce device-resident field samples. CPU mode includes host generation, device allocation and upload. CUDA mode includes device allocation, expansion, stable rejection compaction, status readback and temporary-buffer cleanup.

Engine/NVRTC preparation, seed import, independent CPU oracle generation, result audit readback and result cleanup are outside the timed operation. Both modes retain the same imported key while timed.

Every output and final stream position matches the CPU oracle. Every iteration returns device allocations to the initial baseline. CUDA modes upload no samples and read only one public accepted-count word per batch.
The controller checked all 741 qualified source hashes against committed Git blobs and matched the qualified executable hash before execution; it rechecked source, binary and commit after execution.
limitations: The Rust host and CPU reference are built without optimization; CUDA kernels are compiled by NVRTC. These figures cannot establish an optimized CPU-versus-GPU speedup.
This measures only random-field generation and device storage, not a complete wallet proof, recursive aggregation or transactions per hour.
Results are from one desktop RTX 5080 on driver 615.78.08. V100 and other devices remain unmeasured.
